text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — increased p95 latency on /v1/generate in prod-eu cluster detected by synthetic checks. Start time: 2026-03-02T14:10:56Z. Affected percentage: ~18% of requests. Auto-pager fired to #incidents.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-02T14:08Z started -> rollout: runtime-optimizer:v3 -> canary group=5% -> commit=gitsha:9f8a7b6

maria-ng: I'm on-call. pinging runtime and release. initial check: canary nodes show +300ms p95, overall error rate unchanged. tagging leo-rt and sam-ops. @leo-rt @sam-ops

leo-rt: looking. grabbing kernel logs from canary GPU nodes. attaching quick grep output:
```
[14:11:02] kernel_fallback: triggered path=matmul_qcache
[14:11:03] batcher: dropped 12 requests (timeout)
[14:11:05] kvcache: miss rate spike -> inflight token stall
```

sam-ops: I rolled the runtime-optimizer flag via the feature flag system to on for canary at 14:08. Canary still at 5%. Will pause further rollouts.

anya-sre: adding context: yesterday we merged batching heuristics change that lowers max_batch_wait_ms from 20 -> 5 for low-latency targets. Could be interacting.

carlos-pm: customers reporting slow responses in EU. CS pinged us. @eve-customer-success what's the customer impact? priority? :phone:

eve-customer-success: have three customers reporting “generation timeouts” and increased UI spinner. No data exfil. Two are enterprise (SLA). They're asking ETA and whether a rollback is possible.

leo-rt: confirmed kernel fallback logs coincide with deploy timestamp. Fallback path invokes slower reference kernels causing big latency regression. Suspect a kernel selector heuristic in runtime-optimizer:v3 misclassifies these model shapes.

maria-ng: action plan: 1) pause/kill rollout; 2) flip per-canary kill-switch for runtime-optimizer; 3) if kill-switch doesn't improve, prepare rollback to runtime-optimizer:v2; 4) scale canary pool to drain queue and reduce customer impact. Who can flip kill-switch?

sam-ops: I can flip. Doing: `ffctl set runtime-optimizer canary=false --env prod-eu --author sam-ops` -> command executed at 14:16:22

sam-ops: deploy-bot: feature flag flip completed for canary. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Feature flag change detected: runtime-optimizer canary set to false by sam-ops at 2026-03-02T14:16:22Z.

leo-rt: watching canary traces. p95 dropped from +300ms to +60ms within two minutes on flipped nodes. Good sign. But overall still ~120ms elevated because some nodes already migrated to fallback kernels.

maria-ng: Good. Next: avoid rollback if possible. Let's perform targeted node restart to clear kernel fallback states. @leo-rt kick off a rolling restart for the affected canary nodes? Keep under canary pool.

leo-rt: executing rolling restart on canary subset: `kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime-eu-canary -n redwood-prod --selector=canary=true` -> started 14:20:01

james-support: I posted a short customer-facing note in the incident channel: "We're investigating increased generation latency in EU after a recent deploy. Mitigations underway." Should I escalate to account teams for the two SLA customers? @carlos-pm

carlos-pm: Yes escalate now. Eve, please ping the account leads and offer a postmortem and credits if SLA breached. Keep messaging minimal.

eve-customer-success: Called both account leads at 14:22, left brief message. They asked for ETA — gave 30 mins contingency. They're okay for now.

incident-bot: Canary rolling restart completed 14:25:10. Telemetry shows p95 near baseline on restarted nodes.

leo-rt: overall p95 trending down but still noisy. I see batching controller logs showing backlog because some nodes still using fallback kernels with degraded throughput. Key mitigation: re-evaluate batching heuristics rollback. Will submit a hotfix to restore max_batch_wait_ms=20 on all prod nodes. @sam-ops can you push hotfix to batching-controller config?

sam-ops: applying config change: `kubectl apply -f config/batching-controller/prod-eu.yaml --record` -> changed max_batch_wait_ms back to 20 at 14:28:40

leo-rt: after config change, inflight queue drained, throughput recovered. p95 now within 10% of baseline. Error rate stable. No customer timeouts reported in last 10m.

maria-ng: marking current impact as "partial degradation" -> most requests recovered, small percentage still requeueing. Setting incident severity to SEV3. Starting handoff soon. Anyone staying on call for next 45m?

anya-sre: I can stay for handoff. @maria-ng please collect timeline + actions for postmortem.

maria-ng: timeline draft:
- 14:08 deploy runtime-optimizer:v3 to canary (5%)
- 14:10 synthetic alert: p95 spike
- 14:11 kernel fallback and batch drops observed
- 14:16 feature flag kill-switch flipped for runtime-optimizer canary
- 14:20 rolling restart of canary nodes
- 14:28 batching-controller max_batch_wait_ms restored to 20
- 14:30 p95 nearly recovered

carlos-pm: please include customer impact summary and whether any SLA windows were missed. Eve please keep account teams updated and offer credits if needed.

eve-customer-success: will update and wait for final confirmation.

leo-rt: immediate root cause hypothesis: runtime-optimizer:v3 introduced a kernel selection heuristic that produced a mismatch for certain attention shapes. That triggered kernel fallback to slower kernels; combined with aggressive batching wait reduction (merged yesterday) created throughput starvation for fallback paths.

sam-ops: follow-ups: revert heuristic change in runtime-optimizer, add E2E test for kernel selection across our common model shapes, and ensure feature flag exposes an automated rollback if p95 > threshold within 10 minutes.

maria-ng: Handoff to @anya-sre at 14:40. Remaining tasks for oncall: continue monitoring for 60m, confirm no SLA breaches, and update incident doc. If regressions reappear, escalate for rollback to runtime-optimizer:v2.

anya-sre: taking over. Quick status: p95=+8% vs baseline, no errors, collectors show no further kernel fallbacks. I'll run a deeper pass on telemetry to ensure no hidden regressions.

incident-bot: On-call handoff: from maria-ng to anya-sre at 2026-03-02T14:40:00Z. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.

maria-ng: adding postmortem owners: leo-rt (runtime), sam-ops (release), carlos-pm (customer comms). I'll file a postmortem doc in /postmortems and link to this thread. Closing active paging.

james-support: closing the customer advisory after Eve confirms account leads updated.

maria-ng: quick note for follow-up doc: include timelines, config diffs, precise metrics (p50/p95/p99), list of affected customers, and remediation plan (hotfix + tests + automated rollback). Assign remediation tickets with P1->P3 accordingly.

leo-rt: one more technical note for the postmortem: include these log snippets and the kernel selector config diff. Also propose adding a canary health check that measures kernel fallback rate as a first-class metric.

anya-sre: acknowledged. I will keep monitoring until 15:40, then fully hand back to rotation.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied; monitoring only. Incident channel will be archived after final checks.

maria-ng: thanks everyone. Great quick coordination. :heart:
